newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Pegasus sees debt ratio fall after listing.
newsitem.headline: HK's Pegasus sees debt ratio fall after listing.

text.p: The debt ratio of Hong Kong sports shoe maker Pegasus Holdings Ltd will be substantially lowered to below 50 percent from 85 percent following listing, the company's financial controller Derek Lee said on Monday.
From the net proceeds of HK$182 million to be raised from the public offering, about HK$39 million will be used for repayment of bank borrowings, the company said.

It said HK$34 million would be used to expand production facilities in its plant in China's Panyu, HK$18 million for adding four more production lines in Panyu bringing the total to to 27 lines, and some HK$32 million would be for construction of buildings and structures to match the additional facilities.
Pegasus plans to offer 180.30 million new shares, or 25 percent of the expanded share capital, at HK$1.08 each.
The company said its sales to the North America and European markets representing about 69 and 8.0 percent of the company's turnover for the year ended December 31, 1995.
Pegasus makes athletic footwear, sports sandals and leisure-wear shoes. Its major custmers incllude Nike, Airwalk, Simple, Teva, Dr Scholl's, Guess and Hang Ten.
Yuanta Securities (Hong Kong) Co Ltd is the sponsor and manager of the issue.
